title: METAL: Caching Multi-level Indexes in Domain-Specific Architectures
problem: Domain-specific architectures using index structures for sparse data suffer from cache thrashing due to dynamic pointer-chasing and walk-and-search operations that inflate working set and reduce DRAM efficiency.
motivation: Index structures provide space-efficient sparse data representation and reduce DRAM bandwidth requirements, but their dynamic access patterns cause cache inefficiency if not properly managed.
method: The paper proposes cache organization redesigns to optimize multi-level index traversals in DSAs, addressing pointer-chasing and irregular access patterns through specialized caching that reduces working set expansion and improves data reuse across index levels.
key_novelty: Identifying cache organization as the fundamental bottleneck for index performance in DSAs and designing specialized cache strategies for multi-level index traversals.
contributions: Analysis of cache thrashing issues with sparse index structures in domain-specific architectures
Cache organization and hardware design optimizations for multi-level index operations
Techniques for reducing working set and improving DRAM bandwidth efficiency with sparse indexes
primary_theme: Cache design for sparse multi-level indexes
